note: Recorded facts for the SqPack common header, captured from a real FFXIV install. No Square Enix bytes: only parsed field values, file lengths, and a sha256 of each header's first 1024 bytes. The values were produced by a separate implementation of the format (a throwaway Python reader), never by this crate, so what the gated test proves is agreement between two readers rather than a program agreeing with itself. The hermetic test reconstructs each header's identifying prefix from these fields and asserts the parser reproduces them; the install-gated test (APOGEE_SQPACK_REAL_INSTALL) re-reads the real files and confirms the parser and the sha256 still match. All win32 index headers share one sha256 because the common header's first 0x3C0 bytes (and thus its self-hash) are identical across index files; dat0 differs only in its type byte. `version` is the install these values were measured on, as `ffxivgame.ver` spells it. The gated test holds a live tree to them exactly only when it is that patch; on any other it checks the format's own invariants and a floor under each count, so the patch after this one fails on a regression rather than on a length.
